newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt to prosecute over libel of Mubarak sons.
newsitem.headline: Egypt to prosecute over libel of Mubarak sons.

text.p: Egypt will put on trial three Egyptian journalists and three Saudis on charges of libelling the two sons of President Hosni Mubarak, sources at the prosecutor's office said on Saturday.
Last month, Alaa and Gamal Mubarak complained to the prosecutor's office about corruption allegations that appeared in Asharq al-Awsat, a London-based newspaper close to the Saudi Arabian government.
The allegations appeared in an advertisement for the upcoming issue of the newspaper's sister magazine al-Jadida but the publishers withdrew the article at the last moment.

The sources said the prosecutor put on trial Egyptian journalist Sayed Abdel Atti, who confessed to writing the article, and Jadida editors Fawzeya Salama and Gamal Ismail who have since been replaced.

The court will also try Hisham and Mohammed Hafez, the Saudi Arabian publishers of the Asharq al-Awsat, and the newspaper's editor-in-chief Othman al-Omaer. Editors at Asharq al-Awsat were not immediately available to comment.
All six face a maximum penalty of three years in jail and a 750,000 pound ($221,000) fine, the sources added. The trial date has yet to be set.

Crown Prince Abdullah bin Abdul-Aziz of Saudi Arabia came to Egypt last month shortly after Mubarak's sons complained about the article. An Egyptian government newspaper had said his visit aimed at preventing the affair hurting Egypt-Saudi ties.

In a similar case in 1995, Mubarak visited Saudi Arabia to patch up a row over the public flogging in Saudi Arabia of an Egyptian doctor who alleged a Saudi headmaster sexually assaulted his son. The Egyptian press had been severely critical of the way the Saudi authorities treated the doctor.
